paper.title: Multichannel Treatment of Penning Ionization in He* (1s2s, 3S) + Ar with Discretization of the Electronic Continuum
paper.affiliation: Quantum Theory Project, Departments of Chemistry and Physics, University of Florida, Gainesville, Florida 32611, U.S.A.
paper.journal: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry: Quantum Chemistry Symposium
paper.computational_support: Northeast Regional Data Center of the State University System of Florida

research.objective: Perform multichannel calculations of Penning ionization of Ar by He* (1s2s, 3S) using discretization of the electronic continuum, verify the validity of the decoupling approximation (replacing the full matrix scattering equation by a set of two-state equations), and compute Penning electron energy distributions and integral cross sections at thermal energies for comparison with experiment.
research.key_approximation: Discretization of electronic continuum and decoupling approximation (neglect of continuum–continuum couplings, reduction to N two-state problems)

states.initial: He* (1s2s, ³S) + Ar (discrete electronic state, diabatic potential V_d)
states.final: He + Ar⁺ + e⁻ (continuum of electronic states, molecular ion potential V_+)
states.electronic_basis: Discrete state |φ_d⟩ and discretized continuum states |φ_J(E)⟩, J=1…N

quantum_numbers.total_angular_momentum: Not explicitly coupled; electron angular momentum neglected compared to L

potentials.V_d: Diabatic potential for initial discrete state (He* + Ar)
potentials.V_+: Diabatic potential for molecular ion state (He + Ar⁺)
potentials.V_dJ: Coupling matrix element between discrete state and J-th discretized continuum state

theory.framework: Quantum mechanical multichannel scattering theory with discretized electronic continuum
theory.discretization: Continuum divided into N intervals of width Δε; basis functions u_J(E) chosen (details in ref. 16)
theory.matrix_schrodinger_equation: Coupled equations for heavy-particle radial functions χ_i(R) with angular momentum L (Eq. 3), order N+1
theory.couplings: Only discrete–continuum couplings V_dJ included; continuum–continuum couplings V_JK (J≠K) neglected
theory.decoupling_approximation: Replace (N+1)-channel problem by N independent two-state problems (Eq. 10) for each discretized continuum channel
theory.scattering_amplitude: Partial-wave reactive amplitude S^L_fi (Eq. 8) expressed via S-matrix elements S^L_{J} from two-state or full solutions
theory.riccati_method: Matrix Riccati equation for logarithmic derivative of wavefunction, integrated via Johnson algorithm (ref. 18) for efficiency

numerical.method: Matrix Riccati equation propagation using Johnson algorithm (ref. 18); S-matrix constructed directly from asymptotic Riccati solution
numerical.convergence: Ionization probability converges to three figures with N=21 (matrix order 22) for L=0 at 65 meV (Table I); 20 channels sufficient for accurate dynamics
numerical.partial_waves: L = 0, 24, and others; decoupling accuracy independent of L over thermal range
numerical.collision_energies: 36, 65, 95, 125 meV (also 26–80 meV for total cross sections)
numerical.channels: Up to 20 discretized continuum channels (N=20) for full matrix; 19 two-state equations for decoupling approximation
numerical.computational_advantage: Riccati method ~4 times faster than direct matrix Schrödinger integration; slight unitarity deviation ≤1% deemed acceptable

partial_cross_section_per_unit_electron_.units: a.u. (×10⁻⁴) per a.u. of electron energy
partial_cross_section_per_unit_electron_.energy_range: Electron kinetic energy relative to asymptotic V_d–V_+ difference (0.149 a.u.)

penning_electron_energy_distribution.features: Pronounced maximum at high electron energy due to L=23 resonance (centrifugal barrier in final channel)

results.decoupling_validity: Excellent agreement between full (N+1)-channel and N two-state results for all L and E in thermal range; no L-dependence; no E-dependence up to ~125 meV
results.convergence: Ionization probability converges with N≥20 (Table I)
results.electron_distribution: Qualitative agreement with experiment (ref. 1) in shape and peak position; resonance peak at high ε attributed to L=23 partial wave (47% contribution) where final centrifugal barrier aligns with entrance turning point
results.total_cross_section: Agreement with experiment (ref. 2) within 10% for 26–80 meV; potentials limited to low-energy scattering data
results.elastic_scattering: Full matrix solution required for elastic amplitude; decoupling yields N parametric S^L_{f,J} but no single elastic S-matrix

figures.Figure 1: Partial cross section per unit electron energy for L=0 and L=24 at E=65 meV (2.389×10⁻³ a.u.). Solid: 20-channel full matrix; dashed/dot-dashed: 19 two-state decoupling. Shows excellent agreement.
figures.Figure 2: Partial cross section for L=0 at E=36 meV (1.323×10⁻³ a.u.) and 125 meV (4.594×10⁻³ a.u.). Same comparison; decoupling works across energies.
figures.Figure 3: Penning electron energy distribution at E=95 meV (summed over L, decoupling approx.). Arrow marks experimental maximum from ref. 1. Pronounced high-energy peak due to L=23 resonance.
figures.Figure 4: Penning electron energy distribution at E=125 meV. Similar features.
figures.Figure 5: Total Penning ionization cross section vs collision energy (26–80 meV). Solid: this work; dashed: experiment (ref. 2). Agreement within ~10%.
figures.Table I: Convergence of ionization probability |S^L=0_fi|² with number of discretization functions N at E=65 meV. Converges to 8.53×10⁰ for N≥20.

equations.Eq. 1: Ψ = χ_d(R)φ_d + Σ_J χ_J(R)φ_J(E)  (wavefunction expansion in discrete + discretized continuum)
equations.Eq. 3: Matrix Schrödinger equation for heavy-particle radial functions χ_i(R) with angular momentum L, order N+1. Includes kinetic energy, potentials V_d, V_+, couplings V_dJ, and electron kinetic energies E_J.
equations.Eq. 8: S^L_fi = Σ_J U_J(E) S^L_{f,J}  (partial-wave reactive scattering amplitude; U_J(E) probability amplitude for electron energy distribution)
equations.Eq. 9: dσ(E,ε)/dε = (π/k_a²) Σ_L (2L+1) |S^L_fi(E)|²  (ionization cross section per unit electron energy)
equations.Eq. 10: Two-state equations for each J: [V_d, V_dJ; V_dJ, V_+ + E_J] χ_J = E χ_J  (decoupling approximation)

limitations.decoupling_approximation: Accuracy may decrease for certain partial waves as collision energy increases above ~1 eV.
limitations.potentials: Potential forms (well depths, minima) reflect low-energy scattering data only; not reliable for higher energies.
limitations.neglected_couplings: Continuum–continuum couplings V_JK (J≠K) omitted; electron angular momentum neglected compared to L.
limitations.closed_channels: Associative ionization channels (formation of (ArHe)⁺ + e⁻) not included; would affect elastic and PI cross sections and provide vibrational-rotational populations of molecular ion.
limitations.unitarity: S-matrix from Riccati method shows slight deviations from unitarity (≤1%), considered comparable to other approximations.
